order.intro: Your list is ordered by three rules, applied in turn. Here is each rule and what it did today.

rules.title: What is still happening comes first
rules.body: A habit you started fixing during the session goes to the back of the list.
rules.today: None of the five eased during the session, so this rule changed nothing today.

rules.title: Causes before the things they cause
rules.body: When one habit sets up another, working on the first often fixes the second for free. We only put one behind another when your swings show it: the second goes away on the swings where the first does.
rules.today: It could not be tested today. All five showed on every swing (or all but one), so there is no swing without one to compare against.

rules.title: Then the biggest miss first
rules.body: Each habit is measured against a target range. The one that missed by most, for its range, comes first.

workOns.name: Chicken wing
workOns.goal: Your lead arm stays close to your body after impact
workOns.saw: Your lead arm folds after impact — on all 6 swings, steady from first swing to last. Typical lead arm angle from the torso: 106°, against a target of 40° or less.
workOns.why: A folding lead arm shortens your swing where it should be longest, so you lose speed and the clubface wanders.

causes.lead: We couldn't pin down what drives this one today. Here are the possible causes: the ones we couldn't check, and the ones we've ruled out.

rows.title: Ruled out — measured, and fine

workOns.why: When your head dips going back it must come up again in time, or you hit behind the ball.

drills.label: Club across the chest
drills.instruction: Without a ball, hold a club across your chest. Turn to the top and check in a mirror that the shaft tilts down toward the target and your chest sits behind the ball. Ten slow turns.
drills.targets: To feel the upper body staying behind the ball as it turns, rather than tipping toward the target.
drills.note: A short turn often hides inside this one: if the shoulders cannot turn further, the body tips instead.

workOns.cue: At the top, feel your sternum stay over your trail thigh.
workOns.check: Film face-on. At the top your head and chest should sit a little behind the ball, never toward the target.
workOns.target: Lean away from the target at the top: 0° to 24°, on most swings. Today: −2°.
workOns.figureLabel: Each dot is one swing: lean away from the target at the top, in degrees.
workOns.kicker: Work-on 4 of 5  ·  P4, at the top  ·  6 of 7 swings
workOns.coachTerm: Coaches call the habit Reverse spine angle at P4, or “leaning left at the top”, “forward spine angle at the top”.

workOns.name: Sequence not repeatable
workOns.goal: Your body fires the same way every swing
workOns.saw: Your body fires in a different order from swing to swing — read over the whole session, never one swing. Your lead arm's peak timing varied 12.6× ± 4.1 as widely as touring professionals' do.
workOns.why: Skilled players fire their body in the same order swing after swing, and that repeatability is what most clearly sets them apart.

causes.lead: We don't know of a cause for this one yet. Worth talking through with your coach.

workOns.target: Your peak timing repeating within twice the professionals' spread, over a session.
workOns.kicker: Work-on 5 of 5  ·  Over the whole session
workOns.coachTerm: Coaches call the habit Sequence not repeatable, or “timing varies”, “different every swing”.

steps.head: Rehearse without a ball
steps.body: Slow swings, ten at a time, feeling the change. This is where the new move is learned.

steps.head: Small swings with a ball
steps.body: Half swings at half speed. Keep the feel; ignore where the ball goes.

steps.head: Mix it in
steps.body: Full swings: one with the feel, then two normal ones. Film every fifth swing.

steps.head: One thing at a time
steps.body: Stay with work-on 1 until your next session. The rest of the list waits.

numbers.note: Path, face and offline: positive is right of target, negative left (right-handed golfer). Habits: how many of your five work-ons showed on that swing. Typical: the middle value of your seven swings.

about.dates: This report covers your session on Tuesday 20 October 2026 and was prepared on 20 October 2026. If a session is re-analysed, the report is prepared again and carries the new date.
about.measured: 7 swings with a 8 iron, filmed down-the-line and face-on at high frame rate, with every ball measured by a GC Quad. Your body positions are read from the video by pose tracking; the club and ball numbers come from the launch monitor.
about.ranges: Each habit is judged against a target range. Most ranges are coaching judgement, set from what good ball-strikers do; a few come from published measurements. They are not fitted to you. A swing outside the range is not a mistake in itself — it is where the evidence points.
about.notChecked: Some things could not be checked on every swing: chest peak out of sight (7 of 7); club peak drawn, not judged (7 of 7); swing plane not one plane (6 of 7). Nothing in this report depends on them.
